summary.headline: Zaggle Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR423 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% from 10.1% on DICE costs and expensed capitalisation.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to about INR423 crore, while stand-alone revenue grew 18% to about INR390 crore against a soft seasonal Q1. Adjusted EBITDA was about INR34.7 crore (8.2% margin vs 10.1% a year ago), pressured by DICE integration and relocation costs (about INR3 crore in the last two months of the quarter, before any DICE revenue), one-time expenses, a moderation of capitalisation, annual increments and Zagg.Money costs. Management said DICE revenue starts from July 1 (Q2 FY27), reiterated the 40% consolidated growth guidance and a 25% stand-alone target, and pivoted the stated focus to cash flow and calibrated capitalisation. Analysts pressed on the sharp growth slowdown, margin volatility and the lack of explicit EBITDA guidance.

segments.name: Save and Zoyer (stand-alone SaaS and programs)
segments.commentary: Post new income tax regime, wallet additions and per-user wallet increases for new and existing corporates; 73% of new users came from existing corporates. Large retail chain Zoyer rollout: about 2,000 of roughly 19,000 stores onboarded.

segments.name: Propel
segments.commentary: Consolidated Propel margin 7.1%, stand-alone about 5%, including spillover of overriding commissions realised in Q1. Signed Saint Gobain, Supreme Pipes and Phoenix India during the quarter.

segments.name: Fleet (CDG)
segments.commentary: Transactions up 43% YoY and transaction value up 5.8% YoY; annualised spend run-rate about INR100 crore. First contract with an OMC (HPCL, 5-year aggregator agreement for DT Plus).

segments.name: Zagg.Money (Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: Annualised new card acquisition run-rate raised to about 84,000 from 36,000 a quarter earlier; management cited about INR2.5 crore loss on the business. Co-brand launches with PNB and AU Small Finance Bank.

segments.name: DICE (acquired, spend management)
segments.commentary: Acquired as asset purchase for about INR68 crore excl. GST (from INR123 crore initial valuation). About 100 staff relocated from Pune to Hyderabad; revenue from novated contracts only from Q2 FY27. FY26 DICE revenue about INR12 crore; FY27 target INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (rebranding to Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR80 lakh, +65% YoY; B2B business expected to grow about 120%. Management says on track to breakeven this financial year.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: About INR8 crore invested in Unobanc (moneyHOP), which holds an RBI Authorised Dealer Category-II licence for cross-border payments and forex cards.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of about 40% for FY27 reiterated; stand-alone growth target about 25% retained, despite Q1 at 18%.
No explicit EBITDA margin guidance; management said it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 14-15% framed over 5-7 years.
Stand-alone employee costs to rise in Q2 FY27 with DICE staff; other expenses expected to taper from Q2.
Program fee growth expected to improve in coming quarters; management says 10% growth is 'by design' as cash flow optimisation takes priority.
Novation of about 85-plus DICE clients to complete by end of Q2 FY27; full DICE pickup expected from Q3 FY27.
ADGM (Abu Dhabi) subsidiary to be opened in Q2 FY27; Investors Day planned in the coming quarter.
Expects cash flow turnaround to take about 15-18 months.
capex_capacity: Capitalisation moderated in Q1 FY27 ahead of a full policy review, which is being done with auditors and advisers; more clarity promised in coming quarters.
About INR6 crore of product development cost expensed in Q1 for an immediate client-required product; policy to expense more than capitalise over time.
Relocation of about 100 DICE AI professionals from Pune to Hyderabad completed in May-June; final payment-rail integration into DICE software due by Aug 31 or Sept 10.
Project Shiva (Zaggle Brain) to be filed with the exchange in coming months; patent planned.
Fleet rollouts accelerating in CDG programs; HPCL go-live and monetisation expected in later quarters.
demand_pricing: Stand-alone growth of 18% against soft Q1 seasonality; management attributes the slowdown partly to moving high working-capital-cycle banks' customers to other banks (re-carding takes time).
Geopolitical tailwinds for travel cited, but management said spend growth is not the primary focus; cash back share of program fees is.
Revenue per customer about INR10.6 lakh (INR423 crore / about 4,000 customers, management's rough figure).
Marquee wins: Radisson Hotels, SCA, Bikaji Foods, Nuvama Wealth (Save); Diesel Fashion, Navi, Dezerv (Zoyer); DICE clients Hindalco, Bajel, Trident, IDFC First Bank, Lenskart, XpressBees (novated).
86400 signed LankaPay (first international partner), Union Bank of India (Bharat Bill Payment) and Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank.
Management cites a possible limited MDR on high-value merchant transactions under the proposed Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill 2026 as a UPI monetisation tailwind.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth slowed sharply from the 40-50% run-rate, and is the 40% consolidated guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is about 18% of the full year and growth is expected to rise; SaaS revenue from DICE only starts in Q2 while costs were incurred in Q1. Management moved some high working-capital banks' customers to other banks to prioritise cash flow, which slows program fees. Management said it is not moving away from the 40% consolidated guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give EBITDA margin guidance, and how should margins trend from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin is about 8.2% and it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. About INR3 crore of DICE cost came in over the last two months of Q1 with no revenue, since revenue starts July 1.

qa_highlights.question: What were the expensed items that were previously capitalised, and why are they only partly expensed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no selective capitalisation; the company is moving toward expensing more over time, subject to auditor agreement. One immediate client-required product cost about INR6 crore was fully expensed in Q1, and some infra and product development costs are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Has DICE payment-rail integration been completed and will payments revenue come from DICE from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority of integration is done; the last part is due by August 31 or at latest September 10. Management said payments-related DICE revenue from Q3 is certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is revenue per customer, and what is the program fee growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue per customer is about INR10.6 lakh (INR423 crore over about 4,000 customers). Management called the roughly 10% program fee growth 'by design' and said it expects improvement in coming months, with cash flow and calibrated capitalisation prioritised over the program fee number.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 13-15% EBITDA margin target still stand, and when will margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins have been in the 9-10% range for the last eight quarters and the 14-15% target is a 5-7 year aspiration. Cash flow turnaround to positive would take about 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: When will AI become a meaningful revenue driver, and what is the DICE revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal AI use helped cut about 12.5% of the FY26 cost base and reduced feature launch timelines by up to 50%. DICE FY26 revenue was about INR12 crore; FY27 target is INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

risks_watch: Consolidated revenue growth of 28% vs 40% guidance; stand-alone 18% vs about 25% target; Q2 must show DICE SaaS revenue and program fee pickup.
Cash back at 66.3% of program fees vs about 69% in Q4 FY26; re-carding of customers to other banks may take time and slow program fees further.
Capitalisation policy under review with auditors and advisers; further expensing could keep depressing EBITDA margin, and no firm EBITDA guidance yet.
DICE novation of about 85-plus clients due by end Q2 FY27; payment-rail integration due Aug 31 or Sept 10; full pickup from Q3 FY27.
Zagg.Money loss about INR2.5 crore; card acquisition run-rate of about 84,000 must convert to sustained economics.
Cash flow turnaround expected to take 15-18 months; stock price weakness and promoter share buying questioned on the call.

we will guide in the coming quarters about on the EBITDA margin.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term aspirations and AI, but defensive and evasive when pressed on the growth slowdown, margin volatility and guidance; several answers repeated the 40% and 25% targets without new numbers. Analysts' questions on guidance were answered with reassurance rather than quantified updates.
